subject: Graduate Infrastructure Planning and Delivery, Marc Masarate
email_body:
Hello,

I'm applying for the Graduate Infrastructure Planning and Delivery role at Central Highlands Water in Ballarat, advertised on SEEK and on your LiveHire careers board.

In February 2026 I finished an Advanced Diploma of Civil Construction Design covering road, earthworks, pavement and stormwater design in Civil 3D and AutoCAD. I also hold a Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering (Philippines, 2019). From 2019 to 2020 I worked on site in the Philippines as field engineer and project-in-charge, coordinating crews, inspections and progress records.

I am Melton based, hold a White Card, an Australian driver's licence and own transport, and have full working rights until December 2027 on a Subclass 485 visa. I am available for site and regional work across the Central Highlands. I have not worked in an Australian water utility yet, so the planned rotations are the learning path I want.

I've attached my resume and cover letter. Portfolio: https://macdarenz-droid.github.io/Portfolio.

Kind regards,
Marc Darenz Masarate

letter.subject: Application for Graduate Infrastructure Planning and Delivery
paragraphs: I'm applying for the Graduate Infrastructure Planning and Delivery role with Central Highlands Water in Ballarat, advertised on SEEK and on your LiveHire board. The fixed-term graduate path with mentoring and rotations across Infrastructure Planning and Delivery is the structured start I am looking for in Victorian water infrastructure.

In February 2026 I completed an Advanced Diploma of Civil Construction Design at the Albright Institute of Business and Language: road geometry, earthworks, pavement and stormwater drainage design and documentation in AutoCAD and Civil 3D to Australian Standards, with technical reporting, constructability awareness and Before You Dig Australia enquiries. In 2019 I completed a Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering in the Philippines.

From April 2019 to February 2020 I worked on site in the Philippines as project-in-charge on a community hall renovation, coordinating 10 to 15 workers a day with inspections, safety checks and quality monitoring, then as field engineer on subdivision finishing works, tracking procurement and materials and keeping progress records. Those habits of organisation, clear communication and careful records transfer to a graduate rotating through planning and delivery teams.

I have not worked in an Australian water utility yet, and project management on CHW capital programs would be new. I am based in Melton, Victoria, hold a White Card, an Australian driver's licence and own transport, and have full working rights until December 2027 on a Subclass 485 visa. I am available for hybrid Ballarat work and regional travel across the Central Highlands.
My resume is attached and my drawings are at https://macdarenz-droid.github.io/Portfolio. I would be glad to talk about the rotation plan and how a graduate supports your infrastructure program.
